Regular Season Career Regular Season Bryce Harper Bio Fullname: Bryce Aron Max Harper Nickname: Harp Born: 10/16/1992 in Las Vegas, NV Draft: 2010, Washington Nationals, Round: 1, Overall Pick: 1 College: CC of Southern Nevada Debut: 4/28/2012 Relationship(s): brother of Bryan Harper Bryce Aron Max Harper… Married, wife’s name is Kayla; has two sons and two daughters… In 2013, established “Harper’s Heroes,” a foundation that assists families affected by childhood cancer… Was featured on the cover of Sony’s MLB The Show 19 video game… Earned his GED after just two years at Las Vegas High School (Nev.)… Attended College of Southern Nevada… Was featured on the cover of Sports Illustrated in June 2009… His brother Bryan was a left-handed pitcher who pitched in the Minor Leagues from 2011-18… At the age of 17, hit .443 (101-for-228), 23 2B, four 3B, 31 HR, 98 RBI, 39 BB and 20 SB in 66 games for the College of Southern Nevada in the Scenic West Athletic Conference… As the youngest player in the SWAC, posted a .526 OBP and .987 SLG… Led the conference in a number of offensive categories… Was named 2010 SWAC Player of the Year and also earned First-Team SWAC All-Conference status… His 31 HR in 2010 set a College of Southern Nevada single-season mark… In 2009, batted .626 with 14 HR, 55 RBI and 36 SB in 39 games for Las Vegas High School and became the first high school sophomore ever named a Pre-Season First-Team All-American by Baseball America… In 2008, hit .590 with 11 HR and 67 RBI in 38 games as a freshman… Was a member of USA Baseball’s 2009 18U Team that went 8-0 to claim the COPABE Pan Am AAA Championships in Barquisimeto, VZ… Also played in the 2009 AFLAC All-American Game (2009 Jackie Robinson Award presented by AFLAC), the Area Code Games (2008 All-Area Code Team) and International High School Power Showcase Home Run Derby (2009 Ryan Howard Award)… Ranked 1st nationally in the final 2010 Perfect Game class rankings… Played in 2009 Perfect Game All-American Classic and 2008 PG Junior National Showcase… Signed by: Mitch Sokol. 2025 Ranked 10th in the NL in SLG (.487) & AB/HR (18.56)...Named a 2025 Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalist for the second straight season at first base (also a 2019 finalist in RF)...Reached base safely in 113 of his 132 games...Hit at least 25 HR in a season for the seventh time in his career; was his first time doing so in consecutive seasons since 2017-19...Slugged his sixth career Opening Day HR on 3/27 at WSH...Had a season-high 20-game on-base streak from 4/3-23 (18 H, 20 BB)...Collected his 1,000th ML RBI to put the Phillies ahead, 1-0, on 5/16 vs PIT; became the 14th player in MLB history with 1,000 RBI/runs/walks before turning 33 years old (11 are in the HOF)...Went 28 straight plate appearances without a strikeout from 5/18-24...On the 10-day IL from 6/6-29 with right wrist inflammation...Tallied a career-high four XBH on 7/9 at SF; in his 791st game with the Phillies, was the fifth-fastest to 200 doubles in team history...Had two hits (two 2B) in an inning (eighth) for the second time in his career on 7/9 at SF (also, eighth inn. on 7/10/21 at BOS)...From 7/9-23, was the first player in Phillies history with 14 XBH in a 10-game span; slashed .400/.467/1.000...Hit his 350th career home run on 7/23 vs BOS and was the youngest of eight active Major Leaguers to do so at the time...Became the only active player in MLB to reach 500 RBI with multiple teams on 7/28 at CWS (PHI & WSH)...On 8/3 vs DET, became the second-fastest player in Phils history to reach 500 walks with the club (809 games) behind Bobby Abreu (772 games)...Slashed .396/.444/.604 (1.049 OPS) with 10 RBI in 54 PA over a season-high 12-game hitting streak from 8/17-29...Became the first Phillie in the Statcast era (since 2015) with three consecutive HR at 440+ feet (two on 8/18 & 8/28) and was the first player in MLB to accomplish the feat in a single month...In the postseason, started at first base in all four games of the NLDS vs LAD; went 3-for-15 (.200) with a double, three walks and one run...His 14-game hitting streak in Division Series games from 10/12/17-10/4/25 was the second-longest LDS hit streak of all time. 2024 Won his fourth career Silver Slugger Award and finished sixth in NL MVP voting...Became the fourth player in MLB history to win a Silver Slugger at three different positions (OF, 1B, DH), joining Miguel Cabrera, Albert Pujols and Al Oliver...In his first full season at first base, named a 2024 Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalist (also a 2019 finalist in RF)...Named All-MLB Second Team...Ranked third in the NL in 2B (42), fourth in XBH (72), SLG (.525) and OPS (.898), fifth in OBP (.373), eighth in AVG (.285) and fWAR (5.2), tied for eighth in BB (76) and tied for ninth in HR (30)...Ranked second among NL first basemen with eight outs above average and tied for third among NL 1B with five defensive runs saved...Had a 1.122 OPS with RISP (148 PA), a 1.407 OPS with RISP and two outs (48 PA) and a 2.056 OPS with the bases loaded (nine PA, 13 RBI – two GS/two 2B/BB)...His 42 doubles matched his single-season career high from 2021...Received most votes in the NL for his eighth career All-Star selection and was the third Phillies first baseman to earn a fan-elected start (Rose ’81-82, Kruk ’93); went 1-for-3 (2B) on July 16 at Globe Life Field...Became the fourth player in MLB history with five or more ASG starts in the OF to also make an ASG start in the infield (Hank Aaron, Stan Musial, Carl Yastrzemski)...Had his second career three-HR game on April 2 at CIN (also May 6, 2015) and joined Jayson Werth (May 16, 2008) and Dick Allen (Sept. 29, 1968) as the third Phillie with a GS in a three-HR game...Was on the paternity list from April 22-24 and homered in each of his first two games back, April 25-26...Homered in three straight games from May 5-7 for the 11th time in his career and was the fourth Phillie with either a three-run HR or grand slam in three straight games, joining Aaron Altherr in 2017, Mike Schmidt in 1981 and Andy Seminick in 1949...Hit two grand slams in a season (May 7 vs. TOR and April 2 at CIN) for the third time in his career (also 2019 and 2016)...Named NL Player of the Month for May and June (fourth time in his career); first Phillie with monthly honor in consecutive months since Ryan Howard, Aug.-Sept. 2006...Walked twice on June 9 vs. NYM at London Stadium for 1,000th career BB, is the 14th player in MLB history with 1,000 BB, 1,000+ R and 300+ HR in under 1,600 games...Reached base safely in 21 straight games from June 3-24 and went 21 straight PA without a strikeout from June 15-21; it was his longest on-base streak since Sept. 4-28, 2021 (23 games)...Had a 12-game hit streak from June 15-24 (.423/.455/.865, 1.320 OPS), his first double-digit hitting streak since Sept. 4-18, 2021 (14 games)...On the 10-day IL from June 28-July 8 with a left hamstring strain...His HR on July 13 vs. OAK gave him at least one HR against all 30 ML clubs (including a postseason HR vs. HOU in the 2022 World Series)...Recorded his 700th career XBH on July 20 at PIT and became the seventh player in MLB history with 700 XBH, 1,000 runs and 1,000 walks before turning 32 years old...Has played in all 30 active ML ballparks after facing MIN at Target Field from July 22-24...On July 27 vs. CLE, became the 13th player in MLB history with 100+ HR in two or more ballparks (CBP and Nationals Park)...Was the third ever to reach 100 HR at CBP (Howard and Utley)...Reached 3,000 career total bases on Aug. 4 at SEA, the 42nd player in MLB history to reach the mark and the 13th left-handed hitter before age 32...Slashed .333/.529/.750 (1.279 OPS) with three XBH, three RBI, five walks and three runs in four postseason games...Hit his 12th postseason HR as a Phillie in Game 2 of the NLDS vs. NYM on Oct. 6, tied with Kyle Schwarber for most in Phillies history...His 1.153 postseason OPS with PHI is fourth-highest in MLB history with one team (min. 100 PA), after Bonds (SF, 1.195), Gehrig (NYY, 1.214) and Ruth (NYY, 1.285). 2023 Won his third career Silver Slugger Award and finished 12th in NL MVP voting...Was selected as the Phillies nominee for the Hank Aaron Award...Ranked fourth in the NL in PA/BB (6.83), fifth in OBP (.401), sixth in AVG (.293), seventh in OPS (.900) and eighth in walks (80)...Missed the beginning of the season recovering from UCL reconstruction/repair with ulnar nerve transposition on his right elbow and was reinstated from the 10-day IL on 5/2, 160 days after undergoing Tommy John surgery on 11/23/22...Became the sixth active player with 1,500 hits and 300 HR in his first 12 MLB seasons and the 18th player in MLB history to reach those marks before turning 31 years old (last, Miguel Cabrera in 2012)...On 8/30 vs LAA, became the 12th active player to hit 300 career HR and the fourth-youngest to accomplish the feat...Was the fifth player to hit his 300th HR in a Phillies uniform, joining Ryan Howard (9/22/12), Mike Schmidt (8/14/81), Roy Sievers (7/19/63) and Chuck Klein (8/18/41)...Tallied his ninth career 20-HR season after slugging his first HR of the season on 5/6 vs BOS...Appeared in his 1,000th AB at CBP on 5/20, one of 15 players with 1,000+ AB at CBP and one of two Phillies (J.T. Realmuto) to accomplish the feat...Tallied his 1,400th ML hit in his 1,400th career game on 5/23 vs ARI; registered the 5,000th AB of his career on 5/25 at ATL...Reached 900 career walks on 6/11 vs LAD, the fourth-fastest (1416 G) of the seven other active Major Leaguers with 900 walks (Joey Votto, 1319 G; Mike Trout, 1353 G; Carlos Santana, 1364 G)...Reached base safely in a season-high 15 straight games (15 H, 11 BB) from 6/8-25...Played his 500th game in a Phillies uniform on 6/25 vs NYM...Appeared at first base for the first time in his career on 7/21 at CLE, becoming the 25th player in the modern era to play in over 1,400 major league games (1,446th) before making his first career infield start (last, Nelson Cruz in 2021)...Registered his lone multi-HR game of the season on 8/16 at TOR; was the 25th of his career and his eighth as a Phillie...Notched his second career inside-the-park HR on 8/21 vs SF, the first regular season inside-the-park HR by a Phillie since his own on 7/27/21 vs WSH...Had multiple hits in five straight games from 8/21-26 and 6/30-7/5 (3x career, also 9/25-29/12), the first Phillie with multiple 5+ game streaks of 2+ hits in a single season since Jimmy Rollins had two such streaks of six games in 2006...Homered in three straight games twice (10x career), 8/21-23 and 8/28-30...His HR on 8/29 vs LAA (115.7 mph) was his third-hardest-hit HR since 2015 and the 2nd-hardest-hit HR ever by a Phillie in that span, behind his own 116.4 mph HR on 9/24/19; was the hardest-hit HR by a Phillie at CBP in the Statcast era and tied for the fifth-hardest-hit by any player at CBP...His 1.236 OPS (min. 100 PA) and .784 SLG for August were the highest by a Phillie since Gavvy Cravath in 1913 (1.276 OPS) and Mike Schmidt in 1981 (.817 SLG)...Connected for the 1,500th hit of his ML career on 9/12 at ATL; was a first-pitch HR off Joe Jimenez...Slashed .286/.455/.643 (1.098 OPS) over 13 games in the postseason...Clubbed 3 HR in the NLDS vs ATL, giving him 10 career NLDS homers, the most by any player in MLB history...Tied Jayson Werth and Kyle Schwarber for the most postseason HR in Phillies history with his 11th as a Phillie in Game 5 of the NLCS vs ARI (Zac Gallen) on 10/21...Became the fourth player in MLB postseason history to homer on his birthday, 10/16, in Game 1 of the NLCS vs ARI (Zac Gallen), joining Kolten Wong (25, 10/10/15), Evan Longoria (28, 10/7/13) and Willie Aikens (26, 10/14/80)...Stole home in Game 5 of the NLCS vs ARI on 10/21, the 22nd steal of home in postseason history and the first in LCS play since CHI’s Javier Báez in Game 1 of the 2016 NLCS. 2022 Elected as an NL All-Star by the fans to be the starting designated hitter, but did not play due to injury; was his seventh career All-Star selection...Among players with at least 425 PA, his .877 OPS ranked sixth in the NL (11th in MLB)...His 1.182 OPS with RISP ranked first in the NL and third in MLB (min. 100 PA), behind only NYY’s Aaron Judge (1.241) and LAA’s Shohei Ohtani (1.213) ...Slugged 17 HR as a designated hitter, T-1st in the N...(T-4th in MLB)...His .923 OPS on the road ranked third in the N...(min. 200 PA)...Appeared in 51 of the team’s wins, posting a .335/.423/.611 slash line (1.034 OPS) in those games...Per Statcast data, ranked in the 97th percentile in both xBA (expected batting average) and xSLG (expected slugging percentage)...Reached base safely in 38 consecutive games at Citizens Bank Park from 7/23/21-4/9/22, the 2nd-longest on-base streak in the history of CBP (Jimmy Rollins – 44 games, 7/11/04-4/29/05)...Became the eighth player in MLB history to reach 250 HR, 100 steals and 800 walks in his first 10 years, joining Mike Schmidt, Mickey Mantle, Mike Trout, Barry Bonds, Chipper Jones, Jeff Bagwell and Paul Goldschmidt ...Did not play on 5/15 at LAD, snapping his streak of 106 consecutive games played from 7/17/21-5/14/22, 2nd-longest games played streak of his career (longest: 148 games from 8/10/18-7/23/19)...Named NL Player of the Week for the period of 5/9-15, his seventh career N...Player of the Week Award...Had 34 XBH in his first 50 games...Recorded his 24th career multi-HR game on 6/3 vs LAA, his seventh career multi-HR game as a Phillie...Slugged his sixth career grand slam on 6/5 vs LAA (Raise...Iglesias)...Sustained a left thumb fracture after being hit by a pitch on 6/25 at SD and was placed on the 10-day IL on 6/26...Through games of 6/25, ranked second among all NL players in OPS (.985) & SLG (.599), third in XBH (37), fourth in TB (145) and fifth in AVG (.318)...Was transferred to the 60-day I...on 8/18; appeared in two games with Lehigh Valley (AAA) on a rehab assignment and batted .625 (5-8) with two 2B, two HR, six RBI, three runs and two BB...Was reinstated from the 60-day IL on 8/26...On 9/14 at MIA, hit his 100th HR as a member of the Phillies, doing so in his 436th game with the club...Became the 4th-fastest player (in terms of games played) ever to hit 100 career HR as a Phillie, trailing only Ryan Howard (325 G), Jim Thome (384 G) and Chuck Klein (390 G)...Named NLCS MVP after slashing .400/.400/.850 with four runs, fifth XBH (two HR, three 2B) and 5 RBI in five games...Hit the game-winning HR in Game 5 of the NLCS on 10/23 vs SD (two-run HR off Robert Suarez in the eighth inning)...Overall, slashed .349/.414/.746 in 71 postseason plate appearances...His 1.160 OPS ranks 5th in MLB history for a single postseason (min. 70 PA)...His .462 wOBA ranks T-5th all time in a single postseason (min. 70 PA) with Barry Bonds in 2002...Had four game-winning HR, which was the most ever by any player during a single postseason...His 13 XBH in the postseason were the most ever in a single postseason by a Phillie and one XBH shy of the MLB record (14)...Had 22 hits in the postseason, which set a new franchise record for a single postseason (previous record: 17 by Jayson Werth in 2008 and Shane Victorino in 2009)...Slugged his first career World Series HR in Game 3 on11/1 vs HOU (Lance McCullers Jr.) ...Had an 11-game postseason hitting streak from 10/8-28, setting a franchise record for a single postseason...Became the third player in MLB history to collect an XBH in seven consecutive games during a single postseason (10/8-28), joining Devon White (seven G in 1993) and Carlos Beltran (seven G in 2004)...Homered in three consecutive postseason games, 10/14-18, joining Gary Matthews (10/5-8/83) as the only players in franchise history to do so...Following the season, underwent UCL reconstruction/repair with ulnar nerve transposition on his right elbow on 11/23 (Dr. Neal ElAttrache). 2021 Named NL MVP for the second time in his career and became just the 15th player in history to win multiple league MVP awards before his age-29 season...NL recipient of the Hank Aaron Award...Named NL Outstanding Player of the Year by the MLBPA...Named All-MLB First Team...Named a Stan Musial Award winner by the St. Louis Sports Commission in celebration of the year’s greatest moments of sportsmanship and those in sports who embody class and character...Won his second career Silver Slugger Award...Among all MLB players, ranked 1st in OPS (1.044) & SLG (.615), T-1st in doubles (42), 2nd in OBP (.429), 3rd in walks (100), T-3rd in XBH (78), 4th in IBB (14) & times on base (256), 7th in AVG (.309) and T-8th in OF assists (10)...Among all NL players, ranked 1st in doubles, OPS, SLG & XBH, 2nd in OBP & walks, 3rd in AVG, IBB, OF assists & times on base, 6th in HR (35) & runs (101), 7th in total bases (300), T-9th in bunt hits (4) and T-10th in 3-hit games (12)...Finished 2nd among NL position players (3rd in MLB) in WAR (FanGraphs) at 6.6...Was one of two players in MLB with a .300/.400/.600 slash line (other: TOR’s Vladimir Guerrero Jr.)...Joined Ryan Howard (2006, NL MVP), Chuck Klein (4x, 1929-30; 1932-33) and Lefty O’Doul (2x, 1929-30) as the only Phillies players since 1900 to slash .300/.400/.600 (min. 500 PA) in a season...Became only the fourth outfielder in MLB history with at least 100 runs, 100 walks, 40 doubles and 35 home runs in a season, joining Babe Ruth (2x, 1921 & 1923), Stan Musial (1949) and Barry Bonds (1998)...Was just the second Phillie ever to lead MLB in both OPS and SLG, joining Mike Schmidt in 1981 (1.080 OPS, .644 SLG), and the first player to lead MLB in both since MIL’s Christian Yelich in 2019 (1.100 OPS, .671 SLG)...Slashed .338/.476/.713 with 28 doubles, one triple, 20 HR, 50 RBI, 54 runs and 65 walks in 73 games (311 PA) after the All-Star Game...Led MLB in OPS (1.188), SLG (.713), total bases (171) and XBH (49) following the All-Star break...Was the first player in MLB to post a .300/.400/.700 slash line after the All-Star break (min. 300 PA) since Ryan Howard in 2006 and was the first outfielder to do so since Barry Bonds and Sammy Sosa both did so in 2001...Had 49 extra-base hits and 65 walks after the All-Star Game and prior to him, only two other players had as many extra-base hits and walks following an All-Star Game (since 1933): Barry Bonds in 2001 (50 XBH, 89 BB) and Jimmie Foxx in 1938 (52 XBH, 66 BB)...His 49 XBH following the All-Star break set a new franchise record, surpassing Ryan Howard (45 in 2006) and Chase Utley (45 in 2005)...Became the third player in franchise history with at least 20 HR and 60 walks following the All-Star break, joining Mike Schmidt (1983) and Ryan Howard (2006)...Led the NL in Win Probability Added (4.56)...Was the only player in MLB to have two separate on-base streaks of at least 23 games...Had a career-high 42 doubles, surpassing his previous career high of 38 in 2015...Was the first Phillie with at least 75 XBH, 100 runs and100 walks in a season since Ryan Howard in 2006...His 1.130 OPS at Citizens Bank Park was the highest single-season mark ever by a Phillie in the ballpark’s history (since 2004)...Posted the 8th-highest OPS and 9th-highest SLG in a season by a Phillie since 1900 (min. 400 PA)...The Phillies went 55-25 (.688) when he scored a run...Posted his third 35-HR season (others: 2015 and 2019), third 100-run season (others: 2015 and 2018) and fourth 100-walk season (others: 2015-16 and 2018) ...Collected 300 total bases for the second time in his career (other: 338 in 2015)...Recorded double-digit OF assists (10) for the third time in his career (13 in 2013 and 2019)...Reached base safely in each of his first 10 games to start the season; started the previous two seasons with on-base streaks of 22 games (2020) and 21 games (2019)...Became only the second player in franchise history to start three consecutive seasons with an on-base streak of at least 10 games, joining Richie Ashburn (5 straight seasons from 1955-1959)...Reached base safely in eight straight plate appearances (BB, HR, BB, 2B, 1B, 1B, 1B, 1B) from the seventh inning on 4/16 through the fifth inning on 4/19...Recorded his 100th career steal on 4/27 at STL...Was on the IL, 5/23-6/4, with a left forearm contusion...Collected his 500th career XBH (HR off Max Scherzer),6/22 vs WSH; at the time, among active ML players, was the sixth youngest to reach 500 career XBH...Tied his career high with five hits on 7/6 at CHI (also: 4/19/19 at COL)...Had a career-high three SB on 7/23 vs ATL, becoming the fourth Phillies player in the last 60 years to steal 2nd, 3rd and home in a game, joining Larry Bowa on 8/28/70 vs ATL, Pete Rose on 5/11/80 at CIN and Jayson Werth on 5/12/09 vs LAD...Had a 24-game on-base streak from 7/23-8/17...Hit his first career inside-the-park HR on 7/27 vs WSH (Erick Fedde)...Went 27 consecutive plate appearances without a strikeout from 8/1-6...Collected his 250th career double on 8/1 at PIT; also tied his career high with three doubles for the second time (other: 6/24/18 vs PHI)...Hit his 250th career HR on 8/5 at WSH (Joe Ross); at the time, became the fifth-youngest active player to reach 250 HR...Became the 35th player in MLB history to record his 250th career double and 250th career HR in the same season (last: Mike Trout in 2019)...Posted a .337/.455/.776 slash line (1.231 OPS) with 11 doubles, one triple, 10 HR, 25 RBI, 25 runs and 22 walks in 28 August games...In August, became the first Phillie ever to have more than 20 XBH, 20 RBI, 20 runs and 20 walks in a calendar month; the last ML player to do so was NYY’s Aaron Judge in September 2017...His 22 XBH in August, which led MLB, were his most ever in a calendar month...Posted a 14-game hitting streak (.426), his longest as a Phillie, from 9/4-18; it was the second-longest hitting streak of his career (19 G, 7/1-27/17)...Posted a 23-game on-base streak (.520 OBP) from 9/4-28...Had an XBH in seven straight games, 9/11-18, which tied his career-best XBH streak that he set earlier in the season (8/25-31)...Had a 10-game walk streak, 9/18-28, which tied the longest of his career (also: 4/15-25/15 & 5/5-15/16); was the first Phillie to walk in 10 straight games since Pat Burrell in 2007...Recorded his second career game with two OF assists on 9/26 vs PIT (other: 9/13/13 vs PHI)...Started each of the team’s final 72 games...Walked 26 times over his final 25 games (9/7-end of season). 2020 Among all ML players, ranked 1st in walks (49), 2nd in intentional walks (8), T-3rd in times on base (102) and 5th in OBP (.420)...Among all NL players, ranked 2nd in intentional walks, T-3rd in times on base, 4th in OBP, T-6th in bunt hits (2), T-7th in go-ahead RBI (9), 8th in OPS (.962), T-9th in runs (41) and T-10th in SB (8) & triples (2)...Finished 1st in MLB in first-inning HR (6)...Was one of five hitters in the majors with at least 13 HR and eight SB (others: Ronald Acuña Jr., Mookie Betts, José Ramírez and Fernando Tatís Jr.)...Reached base safely in 25 consecutive games from 9/27/19-8/22/20; it was the 3rd-longest on-base streak of his career (best: 27 G in 2017)...Had a 22-game on-base streak to start the year; reached base safely in 21 consecutive games to start the 2019 season...After reaching base safely, 8/20 at TOR (gm 1), became the first player in franchise history to have multiple on-base streaks of 20 games or better to begin a season...Became the first ML player to begin consecutive seasons with an on-base streak of 20 games or better since Rafael Furcal and Albert Pujols did so in 2008-09...On 8/14 vs NYM, hit a walk-off single in the ninth inning, his 12th career walk-off RBI (11th career walk-off hit)...On 8/20 at TOR (gm 1), became the first Phillie to homer in a ML game in Buffalo since Jack Clements on 7/4/1885 (gm 2)...Had 23 runs, 20 RBI and 20 walks in his first 25 games of the season; since 1920 (when RBI became an official stat), only two other Phillies had at least 20 runs, 20 RBI and 20 walks in their first 25 games of a season: Mike Schmidt in 1983 and Von Hayes in 1989...Stole 16 straight bases without being caught from 7/4/19-9/1/20...Was ejected by 1st base umpire Roberto Ortiz in the bottom of the fifth inning on 9/5 at NYM l On 9/7 at NYM, made his first start in CF since 9/29/18 at COL...On 9/17 vs NYM, became just the fourth Phillie ever to homer in the first and second inning of a single game, joining Jimmy Rollins (4/12/07 at NYM), Gary Redus (7/7/86 vs ATL) and Freddy Leach (6/19/28 vs BRO)...Recorded his 21st career multi-HR game and second of the season on 9/23 at WSH (other: 9/17 vs NYM)...
